According to paramedics, the patient was last seen healthy by his family 4 hours earlier, then was found unresponsive and pulseless in the bathroom. clinical_record:
A man in his 60s presented with a 3-month history of intertrigo involving his groin that he had been treating with a combination of clotrimazole cream, 1%, and hydrocortisone cream, 1%. The condition improved, but he then developed bright red, burning and painful nodules around his scrotum. Medical history included prostate cancer, hypertension, anxiety disorder, hyperlipidemia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and diverticulosis. Current medications included omeprazole, alprazolam, amlodipine besylate, atenolol, simvastatin, and valsartan.

clinical_record:
A 55-year-old white woman with a history of diverticulosis and colonic polyps presented with new-onset flulike symptoms followed by low-grade fever, facial crusted plaques, and 4 weeks of bloody and watery diarrhea. Her facial lesions initially presented as ill-defined pink patches over her cheeks and red papules on her forehead. Over the next 4 days, the lesions spread to her chest, abdomen, back, and left buttock, and a single papule appeared on the right lower extremity. Her low-grade fevers and diarrhea persisted throughout this 4-day period.

In the emergency department, she was febrile and tachycardic. clinical_record:
A man in his 60s presented with a lesion on the left lower eyelid. His ocular history was notable for a traumatic icicle injury as a child that resulted in loss of the left eye. He had surgery to place an implant into the eye socket, and approximately 14 years prior underwent a lower eyelid reconstruction. He had excellent prosthesis position without need for refitting or replacement for more than 10 years until recently noting that his ocular prosthesis would spontaneously extrude from his anophthalmic socket.

On examination, he had a small, pearly lesion in the tear trough region of the left lower eyelid that had been growing over the past few months. He had contraction of the conjunctival mucosal tissue across the fornix of the left lower eyelid and increased scleral show of his ocular prosthesis with shortening of his lower eyelid skin. His prosthesis was extruded from his socket due to cicatricial effects causing conjunctival shrinkage and eyelid skin contracture.

A 61-year-old woman presented with worsening dyspnea over the previous six months, with acute exacerbation. Symptoms included dyspnea on exertion, 2-pillow orthopnea, fatigue, dry cough, and bilateral lower limb swelling worse in evenings. One episode of lightheadedness occurred a week before presentation. Medical history included a 20-year history of autoimmune condition with joint involvement, complicated by usual interstitial pneumonia pattern interstitial lung disease four years prior and keratoconjunctivitis sicca. Patient had poor therapeutic adherence due to significant barriers to care. Previous surgeries included tonsillectomy and partial hysterectomy. Non-smoker, no alcohol use.

Vital signs: BP 138/86 mmHg, pulse 85/min, temperature 96.5°F (35.8°C), BMI 16.3 kg/m², respiratory rate 20/min, oxygen saturation 93% on 3L oxygen. Patient was alert but chronically ill-looking and cachectic. Normal breath sounds on auscultation, no increased work of breathing or accessory muscle use. No jugular venous distention, normal heart sounds. Pupils equal and reactive, no conjunctival injection or scleral icterus. No skin rashes, ulcerations, palpable purpura, or nodules. No palpable lymph nodes. Abdomen soft, nontender, nondistended with normal bowel sounds. Muscle tone normal, power 5/5, no cranial nerve deficits. Bilateral ulnar deviation at metacarpophalangeal joints with swan neck deformities at third and fourth fingers bilaterally. No joint swelling, warmth, or redness, but tenderness noted.

clinical_record:
A 30-year-old woman presented with a 15-year history of recurrent ankle swelling and intermittent painful and tender nodules on her legs and feet. Her symptoms worsened during two pregnancies, which were carried to term. One and a half years before admission, she experienced escalation of symptoms, with nodules progressing to painful leg ulcers, and developed intermittent oral and vaginal ulcerations. Previous treatments included wound care, leg compression, systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, aspirin, and rivaroxaban.

Patient had large, extremely tender, irregularly shaped circumferential leg ulcers, with violaceous and purpuric borders, areas of eschar, and a fibrinous base. Reticulated erythema and purpura were present on hands. Faintly erythematous, blanching macules and papules coalescing into patches and thin plaques were observed on bilateral thighs. Genital and oral ulcers were also present.

- Laboratory findings: Elevated C-reactive protein, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, mildly elevated C3, leukocytosis, and hyperglycemia.- Imaging studies:  - Doppler ultrasound of lower extremities showed venous stasis  - Systemic imaging revealed splenomegaly and involvement of retroperitoneal, pelvic, and inguinal lymph nodes- Pathological findings:  - Skin biopsy (left thigh): Monomorphic, perivascular, and periadnexal atypical lymphocytic infiltrate  - Skin biopsy (purpuric edge of leg ulceration): Epidermal necrosis with numerous fibrin thrombi and intra-/perivascular atypical lymphocytic infiltrate showing monotony and hyperchromasia  - Immunohistochemical staining: CD3-positive T cells coexpressing CD4 and CD8 with preserved expression of CD7  - Flow cytometry: Phenotypically abnormal T-cell population with CD52 expression

Vital signs were stable with blood pressure 127/86 mm Hg, heart rate 56 beats/min, respiratory rate 17 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air.

Physical examination findings were unremarkable, without signs of acute heart failure.

clinical_record:
A 65-year-old man with a history of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity presented with several months of facial swelling, dysphagia, and dysarthria. Shortly thereafter, he developed a pruritic rash on his trunk and upper extremities. He did not report a personal or family history of angioedema. His medications included lisinopril, atorvastatin, albuterol, and ibuprofen for rheumatoid arthritis. The patient had discontinued etanercept six months before presentation. He presented to the emergency department two weeks after seeing his primary care provider for a persistent periorbital, chest, and upper extremity rash. His rash worsened, and he noted new throat swelling and weakness.

Vital signs were stable on arrival. Physical examination was notable for anasarca and a diffuse coalescent erythematous rash over the extremities, chest, and abdomen, with scaling and crusting of the back. There was a heliotrope rash and erythematous lip swelling. He had weakness to resistance in all extremities and a muffled voice without tongue swelling. Over several days, the patient's shoulder and hip weakness progressed, and he could not lift his arms above his head or stand without assistance.

- Laboratory Tests:    - Basic metabolic panel and complete blood count were unremarkable    - Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate    - Negative viral respiratory panel    - C4, C1q, and C1 esterase inhibitor were unremarkable    - Normal serum and urine protein electrophoresis    - Elevated transaminases    - Elevated anti-Sjögren syndrome–related antigen A autoantibodies    - High antinuclear antibody titers    - Negative anti-Jo antibody    - Elevated creatine kinase    - Positive myositis panel for anti-SAE antibodies  - Imaging Studies:    - CT neck: Mild submental inflammatory stranding with no discrete fluid collection or abscess    - Liver ultrasound: Hepatic steatosis    - CT chest: Multiple nodular and airspace opacities, including right lower lobe nodule  - Pathology:    - Skin biopsy results were consistent with Wong-type presentation

In May 2020, the patient developed posterior occipital tingling, which worsened with emotional agitation but would subside spontaneously after a few minutes. No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case.
